summary: Leo Strauss was a philosopher who studied at Hamburg, Freiburg, Marburg, and Columbia. His academic posts included Cambridge (~1934-1938), The New School (~1938-1949), the University of Chicago (~1949-1969), Claremont McKenna College (~1968-1973), and St. John's College (~1969-1973).
Leon Hurvitz worked in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He held professorships at the University of Washington (~1955-1971) and the University of British Columbia (~1971-1988).

Linguist Leonard Bloomfield studied at Harvard, Wisconsin-Madison, Chicago under Francis A. Wood and Carl Darling Buck, Leipzig, and Göttingen. He held posts at Illinois Urbana-Champaign (1910-1921), Ohio State (1921-1927), Chicago (1927-1940), and Yale (1940-1949).
Leonard Blussé, a scholar in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Japanology, studied at Leiden University (~1970-1986) and later held a post there from 1998 to 2011.
Leonard C. D. C. Priestley, working in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology, studied under A. K. Warder and F. E. L. Priestley. He held a post at the University of Toronto (attested 1991).

Religious studies scholar Leonard Swidler studied at St. Norbert College, Saint Paul Seminary, Marquette, Wisconsin-Madison, Tübingen, and Munich. He taught at Duquesne University (1960-1966) and served as professor at Temple University from 1966 to 2022.

id: P:Leonard W. J. van der Kuijp
summary: Leonard W. J. van der Kuijp, a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies, earned his doctorates at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen. He held posts at the University of Washington (~1990-1995) and Harvard University (appointed chair 1995).
Leonid Kulikov works in Indology and linguistics. He has held academic posts at Leiden University (attested 2007) and Ghent University (attested 2026).

Leopold Pospisil studied at Charles University, Willamette University, the University of Oregon, and Yale University. He served as a professor at Yale University from 1956 and curator at the Peabody Museum of Natural History (~1956-1993).

Indologist Leopold von Schroeder studied at Tartu, Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth, and Jena. He held academic posts at the University of Tartu (1882, 1890), the University of Innsbruck (1896), and the University of Vienna (1899).

Leslie S. Kawamura was a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at the University of Saskatchewan under Herbert V. Guenther. He served as a professor at the University of Calgary from ~1976 to 2010.

Levi McLaughlin, a scholar of Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies, studied at the University of Tokyo and Princeton University. His appointments include Kokugakuin University, Wofford College, the University of Iowa, and North Carolina State University (2012).

Lewis Doney, a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and history, studied under Ulrich Pagel and earned a PhD from SOAS University of London. He held posts at the University of Munich (attested 2018) and the University of Bonn (attested 2021).

Lewis Hodous, who worked in Sinology and Buddhist studies, studied at Case Western Reserve, Hartford Seminary, and Halle-Wittenberg. He held leadership posts at Fukien Union Theological Seminary (1902-1917) and taught at Hartford Seminary (1917-1945).

Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar Lewis R. Lancaster studied at Roanoke, Claremont, and Wisconsin-Madison under Richard Hugh Robinson. He held long-term positions at the University of California, Berkeley (attested 1974-1996, 2012) and the University of the West (1992).

id: P:Lha Zang Lama Rigdzin Gar Gyi Wangchuk
summary: Lha Zang Lama Rigdzin Gar Gyi Wangchuk studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé, Patrul Rinpoche, and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.

Tibetology scholar Lhagpa Phuntshogs served as president of the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences (1983-1991), secretary-general of the China Society of the Tibet Plateau (1991-2000), and director general of the China Tibetology Research Center (2000).
Lhakpa Tsering, working in Tibetology and linguistics, has served as a professor at Tibet University and an assistant professor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 2026).

Li-ching Chang, working in Sinology and linguistics, taught Mandarin Chinese at Tunghai University (~1961-1964), the University of Washington (~1965-1968), and the University of Pennsylvania (~1980-2005), as well as Bryn Mawr, Harvard, and Swarthmore.
Liang Cai, a scholar in Sinology, history, and archaeology, studied under Daniel Boucher and held a post as a junior scholar at the University of Arkansas (attested 2014).
